rationale: The Latin anchors *pittacium* (patch, rag, label), *commissura* (joint, seam), and *lamina* (thin plate, sheet) all point to a sense of "patch, piece of cloth/metal, or thin plate" — i.e. a piece of material used for patching or covering. None of the four WordNet candidates capture this sense: clout.n.01 is an archery target, pull.n.03 is influence, clout_nail.n.01 is a type of nail, and punch.n.01 is a blow. The Old English CLÚT in this definition refers to a patch or piece of cloth/metal, which has no suitable WordNet analog among the candidates.
